Your units are advancing through SIL and RUH toward my border. I will defend my centers and will not leave the Balkan flank exposed. Are you willing to halt eastward moves and keep out of Turkish centers this fall? If not, state your intended moves so I can plan accordingly.

I kept my forces out of WAR, MOS, STP and SEV in spring, and A GAL has left your claimed ground. Please keep A WAR, A MOS and A LVN away from my centers again this fall. What are your intended moves, especially A WAR and A LVN?

England to Russia, Fall 1932: Agreed that F NOR, F SWE and A KIE stay off STP and the Baltic while A MOS and A WAR stay out of DEN, HOL and SWE. I will not send units toward your centres. Against Turkey, I am open to coordinating once I see your spring and fall moves against Galicia and Rumania. Keep your word on the north.

England to Italy, Fall 1932: I cannot commit units east this fall; my fleets are needed to hold the North Sea and Channel. Turkey is your problem as much as ours. Your best path is A VEN or A GRE pressing Turkish Trieste or Serbia. Keep your fleets out of English waters and I will do the same.

England to France, Fall 1932: The western truce stands. No English units into BEL, PIC or BRE, and no French units into ENG, HOL, DEN, KIE, NTH or BER. I am not moving east this fall, but I will not assist Turkey in any way. Keep your word in the Channel and we stay at peace.
A SIL will move to BOH to contest the Turkish unit there. A RUH will move to BUR, not into Russian centers. If you can, contest Turkish advances toward GAL or UKR; I’ll keep clear of your centers.

A SIL will attack BOH this fall; A RUH will move to BUR. Please have A TRI attack BUD if you can, and keep A MAR and F TYS out of Italian centers as agreed. We need to make Turkey defend its central flank.

I will not halt the eastward pressure while you hold BOH and advance through the Balkans. A SIL is moving to BOH; A RUH will move to BUR. I will keep French units out of Turkish supply centers this fall where possible, but I will not promise to abandon the front.

I won’t promise to vacate TRI while the Turkish army is advancing through central Europe. My priority is containing that advance, not pressing west. I’ll keep A GRE and A VEN out of Turkish centers, but cannot guarantee a quiet border while your units threaten my position.

I’ll keep A MAR and F TYS safe from Italian moves. A GRE can move against SER with A TRI supporting; that gives us pressure on the Turkish Balkan position. I can’t commit A TRI to BUD while it holds TRI, but your A SIL toward BOH will help contain Turkey.

Russia to Italy: Fall 1932. I cannot defend the south alone while Turkey holds BUD, VIE and BUL. My A WAR and A MOS will contest Ukraine and Galicia, not the Adriatic. Keep A TRI and A GRE pressing Turkish holdings in Serbia and Rumania if you can, and I will keep Russian units away from your Mediterranean centres.

Russia to Turkey: Fall 1932. Your A UKR and A BOH have pushed into my lines, and I see no written reply on UKR leaving Russian ground. My A WAR and A MOS stay put this fall, but I will not guarantee more. Withdraw A UKR from Russian-claimed ground and keep A TYR out of MUN, then we can talk about ANK, BUL and CON.

Russia to France: Fall 1932. Agreed that we both stay out of each other's centres while Turkey is the target. I will keep A MOS and A WAR off MUN and BUR this fall. If your A SIL moves toward BOH, I will support pressure on Turkish forces in Galicia and Ukraine, not against you. Please keep A MUN-area moves clear of Russian centres.

I have no intention of sending fleets to ENG or NTH. F AEG and F ION are committed to the eastern Mediterranean, not your centers. A BOH will defend my central position; A TYR will not enter KIE or other English-held centers this fall. I propose we keep the northern seas quiet while I deal with the continental threats.

A UKR will not move into WAR or MOS this fall, and A TYR will not enter MUN. I cannot promise to abandon UKR, which is essential to my defense. Keep A WAR and A MOS out of ANK, BUL, and CON; tell me whether you intend to hold WAR and MOS or advance elsewhere.

England to Turkey, Spring 1933: You now hold 12 centres and lead by a wide margin, which worries the rest of us. I want a clear answer: will your fleets or A TYR, A BOH, A MUN move against any English-held centre (DEN, KIE, HOL, NOR, SWE) this year? If you pledge to stay away from the North and Channel, I will keep my fleets home too.

Turkey is now at 12 centers and needs only six more to win. Please keep the western truce, but can you apply pressure in the north—especially with F SWE toward STP or A KIE toward MUN—rather than leave Turkey free to consolidate?

Turkey has reached 12 centers. I’ll keep F TYS out of Italian centers and press from BOH/BUR. Can A VEN support A BOH into TYR, and can you use A TRI or A GRE to contest BUD or SER? Please tell me your intended moves.

Turkey is at 12 and must be stopped. Please use A WAR and A MOS to contest UKR or GAL this spring. I’ll keep French armies out of Russian centers; can you coordinate against Turkey’s forces around GAL and the central front?

Turkey is at 12 and can win with six more. Let’s coordinate directly against its central line: what are A BOH and A BUR doing this spring? I can use A BUD, A VEN, and A ALB to pressure Turkish units, but need to know your targets so we don’t waste force or open our border.

Turkey is six centers from victory. Please tell me whether A MOS and A WAR can contest Ukraine or Galicia this spring, and your intended destinations. I can apply pressure from BUD and the Balkans; coordination may force Turkey to defend instead of expanding.

You are now six centers from an immediate solo win. State whether A MUN, A TYR, A GAL, or your southern units intend to enter Italian centers this spring. I will defend my position and coordinate against any advance; if you keep clear of Italy, we can discuss a temporary quiet border.

Russia to Turkey, Spring 1933: You hold 12 centres and A GAL, A TYR, A MUN are on my border. I need written confirmation that A MUN and A TYR stay out of WAR, MOS, UKR-held Russian ground and STP. Name your spring moves for A GAL and F RUM, and I will state mine for A WAR and A MOS.

Russia to England, Spring 1933: Our northern pact holds if F NOR, F SWE, A KIE and F BAL stay off STP, Baltic and my centres. I will keep A MOS and A WAR off DEN, HOL, SWE. Turkey at 12 is the danger to both of us. Share your spring orders and I will share mine.

Russia to France, Spring 1933: Turkey is the leader and must be checked. I will keep A MOS and A WAR out of MUN and BUR. Please keep your armies out of WAR, MOS and STP. If you press A BOH or TYR against Turkish units, I can pressure GAL from the north.

Turkey is at 12 and must expand quickly. I propose we avoid fighting each other this spring: I will keep A TYR out of VEN and F NAP out of ROM if you keep A BUD and A VEN out of Turkish centers. What are your plans for GRE, VEN, and TUN? France’s advance is a threat to both of us.

Your units in BOH and BUR threaten my position, and I will defend it. To avoid a costly front, will you halt eastward advances and keep clear of Turkish centers this spring? State your plans for A BOH, A BUR, and F TYS.

Would England coordinate pressure on France while Turkey handles the southern front? I will keep my fleets away from ENG and NTH. Please tell me your plans for the French-held centers and whether you can move against France this spring.

England to Russia, Spring 1933: The northern pact stands. F NOR, F SWE, A KIE and F BAL stay off STP, the Baltic and your centres. Turkey at 12 is the real danger. I'll hold my northern units this spring. Please show me your Galicia and Rumania moves, and let's coordinate against Turkey's southern centres next season.

I’ll keep A BOH and A BUR out of Russian centers. Please use A WAR and A MOS to contest GAL/UKR; pressure on GAL will help pin Turkey while I challenge its central position. I’ll share my exact moves after we coordinate with Italy.

I won’t halt the eastward pressure while you hold 12 centers and threaten a solo. A BOH and A BUR will remain directed against your central front, not Turkish centers this spring. F TYS will stay clear of Italian centers.

A BOH can press toward TYR, and A BUR can move to support pressure on the Turkish central line. Please use A VEN to support A BOH into TYR if possible, and have A TRI or A GRE contest BUD/SER. I’ll keep F TYS out of Italian centers.

I will not promise a quiet border while you are six centers from victory. My A VEN will support France’s A BOH into TYR, and A BUD with A ALB will pressure SER. F TUN will move to ION. I have no intention of entering your centers with A VEN, but I will oppose your expansion.

I’ll have A VEN support A BOH–TYR, and A BUD attack SER with A ALB supporting. I have no A TRI or A GRE to commit. F TUN will move to ION; F SPA/SOUTH and A TUS will stay clear of French centers. Please keep F TYS out of Italian centers as agreed.

Russia to France: Turkey is the real threat, so I will push A WAR toward Galicia and Ukraine this spring and keep A MOS off MUN and BUR. Please keep your armies out of WAR, MOS and STP, and press A BOH or TYR against Turkish units. Tell me your exact moves so we do not collide.

Russia to Italy: A WAR and A MOS will contest Galicia and Ukraine this spring, not the Adriatic. I need both units to hold Russian centres first, so my southern help is limited. Keep pressing BUD, SER and the Balkans against Turkey, and I will keep Russian units away from your centres.

I will keep my fleets out of ENG and NTH this spring. I cannot pledge that A TYR, A BOH, or A MUN will stay away from English-held centers; my units must respond to the continental position. I have no specific move against DEN, KIE, HOL, NOR, or SWE to offer you. France remains the common obstacle—please press its centers.

A MUN and A TYR will not enter WAR, MOS, or STP this spring. A GAL will move to BOH, and F RUM will support A GAL to BOH. I will not promise to leave UKR-held ground. State whether A WAR and A MOS will hold or move, and keep them away from ANK, BUL, and CON.

I will keep A TYR out of VEN and F NAP out of ROM this spring; I am not committing A MUN or A GAL to Italian centers either. My southern units are focused on the eastern front, not an attack on GRE, VEN, or TUN. Keep A BUD and A VEN out of Turkish centers, and we can avoid a costly fight.

England to Turkey, Fall 1933: Your A TYR retreated to TRI and you hold 12 centres. Stay out of DEN, KIE, HOL, NOR and SWE, and I will keep my fleets off the Mediterranean approaches and your Balkan centres. Confirm this in writing or we both need to plan for conflict.

England to France, Fall 1933: The western truce stands if you keep F TYS and A PIC out of ENG, BEL-adjacent English interests and Channel waters. Turkey at 12 is the shared danger. Tell me whether you will hold BER and MUN-facing units defensively this fall.

England to Russia, Fall 1933: The northern pact stands: F NOR, F SWE, A KIE and F BAL stay off STP, the Baltic and your centres, and A MOS and A WAR stay out of DEN, HOL and SWE. Turkey must be contained. Share your fall orders against Rumania and Galicia.

Turkey has 12 and is one strong season from a solo. Can we coordinate now? I can use A TYR to attack TRI; please use A VEN to support TYR–TRI if legal, and tell me your plans for A SER and A ALB. I’ll keep F TYS clear of Italian centers.

Turkey is at 12; we need immediate pressure to prevent a solo. Can F SWE move against STP, and can your northern units support or otherwise contest Turkey’s northern position? I’ll keep to our western truce. Please tell me what you can commit this fall.

Turkey is at 12 and must be stopped. What are A WAR and A SEV doing this fall? Please contest Turkish forces in GAL/UKR or attack an exposed Turkish center; I’ll press from TYR and keep French units out of Russian centers.

Turkey remains six centers from victory. I can use A SER and A ALB to pressure Turkish-held Balkan centers this fall; please use A TYR and A RUH against its central line. Which Turkish target will you attack, and can we coordinate without opening our border?

Turkey is still six centers from a solo win. Can A WAR or A MOS contest a Turkish-held center this fall, or are both needed to defend? I can pressure from A SER/A ALB, but need to know whether you can threaten Galicia or Ukraine.

Turkey is six centers from victory. Can you use F BAL or another unit to pressure a Turkish-held northern center this fall, especially STP, or are your units committed elsewhere? I can press from the Balkans and want to coordinate rather than leave Turkey free to expand.

Russia to Turkey, Fall 1933: You are at 12 and I cannot let you run over the board. Name your fall moves for A GAL, A TYR, A TRI and F RUM. If you move any unit into WAR, MOS, SEV or STP, we are at war. Keep A ARM and A SMY away from my southern centres and I will keep A SEV and A WAR defensive.

Turkey will keep its fleets out of ENG and NTH this fall. France remains the immediate obstacle to my expansion; will you press French centers rather than intervene against my forces in central Europe? Please state your intended moves around BER, KIE, and HOL.

Your forces at BOH and RUH threaten my position, and I will defend it. I propose a limited fall de-escalation: keep your units out of Turkish centers and do not support an attack on TRI or VIE; I will avoid advancing into your centers this fall. What are A BOH, A RUH, and A TYR doing?

I propose we stop spending units on the Turkish-Italian border while France threatens both of us. Keep A BUD and A VEN out of Turkish centers and do not support attacks on my units; I will not direct A TYR or the southern fleets against Italian centers this fall. What are your plans for SER, VEN, and ION?

England to France: The western truce stands while your units stay out of ENG, NTH, HOL, DEN, KIE and BER. I will not move into BEL or PIC. Turkey is the bigger threat, but I will not open a northern front against you this fall. Keep F TYS away from our Channel waters and we remain at peace.

England to Italy: My fleets are committed to the North Sea and Channel this fall, so F BAL will not reach STP. I cannot spare a unit for Turkey this year. Press from the Balkans with A VEN and A SER toward TRI, BUD or GRE, and keep your fleets out of English waters. We can coordinate next year.

England to Turkey: Your fleets staying out of ENG and NTH is noted. I will not move into the Balkans or Mediterranean approaches against you. But I need your written commitment: no army or fleet into DEN, KIE, HOL, NOR or SWE. A TYR retreat to TRI and A MUN are a concern. Confirm and we remain at peace.

The truce stands: F TYS and A PIC will stay out of English centers and the Channel. I’ll hold BER and keep A RUH defensive against MUN. Please commit F SWE toward STP or otherwise pressure Turkey’s northern line; delaying Turkey is urgent.

I’ll use A TYR to attack TRI and A RUH to support that attack. Please support A TYR–TRI with A VEN if legal, and use A SER and A ALB to pressure Turkish-held Balkan centers. I’ll keep F TYS clear of Italian centers.

I won’t agree to de-escalation while you hold 12 centers. A BOH will stay directed against your central line, A RUH will support pressure on TRI, and A TYR will attack TRI. I will avoid Turkish centers otherwise and keep F TYS clear of Italian centers.

I’ll support A TYR–TRI with A VEN. A SER and A ALB can combine against A GRE: I plan A ALB–GRE with A SER supporting. This keeps pressure on Turkey without opening our border; please use A RUH or another unit to reinforce the attack on TRI if you can.

I won’t agree to leave your expansion unopposed. I intend to keep pressure on your Balkan line with A SER and A ALB, and A VEN will support France’s move against TRI. F ION will remain in the eastern Mediterranean; I’m not directing it against Italian centers.

Russia to England, Fall 1933: The northern pact holds from my side: A MOS and A WAR stay out of DEN, HOL and SWE. Against Turkey, I will decide my fall moves once I see Turkey's answer on GAL, TYR and TRI. Keep F NOR, F SWE, A KIE and F BAL off STP and the Baltic, as agreed.

Russia to France, Fall 1933: A WAR and A SEV will hold defensively this fall, not attack. I will not move into MUN, BUR or your centres. Press TYR and Turkish units from the west, and tell me exactly what A TYR and A BOH do so we do not collide. I can pressure GAL only if Turkey moves into WAR or UKR.

Russia to Italy, Fall 1933: A WAR and A MOS are needed to hold my own centres this fall, so I cannot threaten Galicia or Ukraine yet. Keep pressing Turkey in the Balkans with A SER and A ALB; Turkish centres BUD and TRI are your best targets. I will keep Russian units away from your centres.

A GAL will hold, A TYR will defend TRI, and A TRI will hold; F RUM will support A TRI. None will move into WAR, MOS, SEV, or STP. Keep A SEV and A WAR defensive and away from my centers, and we can avoid opening another front.

Turkey will keep its fleets out of ENG and NTH, but I cannot pledge to stay away from every English-held centre while France and Italy contest my central position. I have no specific order against DEN, KIE, HOL, NOR, or SWE this fall. Please keep your fleets off my Mediterranean approaches and Balkan centres.

England to Turkey, Spring 1934: You hold 12 centres and your A TYR and A MUN sit close to our North Sea holdings. Pledge in writing that no Turkish unit enters DEN, KIE, HOL, NOR or SWE, and I will keep F BAL, F NOR and F SWE out of STP and your Balkan approaches. Silence will be read as refusal.

England to Russia, Spring 1934: The northern pact still stands. I will keep F NOR, F SWE, A KIE and F BAL off STP and your centres. Turkey now holds 12 and is the real threat. Will A WAR and A MOS hit Turkish Galicia or Rumania this spring? Tell me your moves.

England to France, Spring 1934: The western truce stands: no English units into BEL, PIC, BRE, and I expect none of yours into ENG, NTH, HOL, DEN, KIE or BER. Turkey leads at 12, so let us both keep pressure on the Continent rather than fight each other. Confirm your F TYS stays out of the Channel.

Let’s hit Turkey’s central line together. I propose A TRI–VIE, with A VEN supporting TRI–VIE. Can A GRE move to BUL or otherwise pressure Turkey’s Balkan centers, and can A SER contest BUD? I’ll keep F TYS clear of Italian centers.

Turkey still needs only six centers to win. Please commit your northern forces to pressure its holdings: F NOR toward the Barents Sea and onward toward STP, and F SWE toward BOT or another useful northern position. I’ll keep to our western truce.

With only A WAR available, please attack GAL if legal or move toward a Turkish-held position rather than hold passively. I’m coordinating pressure on VIE from TRI with Italy. I’ll keep French units out of Russian centers.

Turkey is still six centers from a solo. I can send A SER–BUD, A GRE–SER, and A VEN–TYR to pressure its line, but need your plan for A TYR, A RUH, and A TRI. Please keep A TRI out of Italian centers and coordinate a concrete target with me.

Your 12-center position remains an immediate danger to everyone. I will not promise a quiet border while you can win by taking six more centers. What are A TYR, A UKR, and your Balkan units doing this spring? I intend to contest your expansion.

Turkey remains six centers from victory. Can any English unit threaten a Turkish center this spring, or will your forces stay committed in the north? I am pressing from the Balkans; please keep F BAL and your other fleets clear of Italian centers.

Russia to Turkey, Spring 1934: You hold 12 centres and I hold only WAR. Stating plainly: A MOS and A WAR will hold this spring, not enter your centres. Confirm A ARM, A SYR, A UKR and A VIE stay out of WAR, MOS, SEV and STP. Will you keep F BLA off SEV?

Russia to France, Spring 1934: Turkey at 12 is the shared danger. My A WAR and A MOS will hold. Please confirm your A BUR, A RUH and A TRI moves so we avoid collisions, and that no French unit enters WAR, MOS or STP. Let's jointly pressure Turkish TYR or VIE in the fall.

Russia to England, Spring 1934: The northern pact stands. F NOR, F SWE, A KIE and F BAL must stay off STP, the Baltic and my centres. A MOS and A WAR will stay out of DEN, HOL and SWE. Turkey is the threat; share your spring orders so we both know where Turkish pressure is aimed.

Turkey needs to stop France’s eastward pressure before it costs us both. Will you move against French-held BER or support pressure on French centers this spring? My forces are focused on the central and southern fronts; I will keep my fleets out of ENG and NTH.

Your forces at BUR, PIC, RUH and TRI threaten my position. I propose a limited spring stand-down: keep your armies out of VIE and TRI and do not support attacks there; I will not advance into French-held centers this turn. What are your plans for A BUR, A RUH, and A TRI?

France remains a threat to both of us. I propose we avoid attacking each other’s centers this spring: keep A SER and A VEN out of Turkish centers, and I will keep A TYR and F ROM clear of Italian centers. Are you willing to hold the Balkan line while pressing France?

England to Italy: I cannot spare F BAL for Turkey this spring; my northern fleets are tied up holding our centres. Keep your fleets out of English waters and press Turkish centres in the Balkans. If Turkey overextends, we can talk about a joint push next year.

England to Russia: The northern pact stands from my side. F NOR, F SWE, A KIE and F BAL stay off STP, the Baltic and your centres. I am not sending units south this spring. Turkey at 12 is the danger to us both, so please press its Galicia and Rumania positions with A WAR and A MOS.

England to Turkey: I will not give a blanket promise on central Europe while A TYR and A MUN sit beside our holdings. My written pledge: I will not attack Turkish centres in the Balkans or Mediterranean this spring. Keep DEN, KIE, HOL, NOR and SWE clear and we remain at peace.

England to France: I will not move into BEL, PIC, BRE or the Channel, and I expect F TYS to stay out of ENG. I am not moving F NOR or F SWE toward STP, since my northern units are needed at home. Keep your forces on Germany and Italy and we stay at peace.

Confirmed: F TYS stays out of the Channel. I’ll honor the western truce and keep my units out of your listed interests. Please use F NOR toward the Barents Sea and F SWE toward BOT/STP to pressure Turkey; its 12 centers make delay urgent.

A TRI–VIE cannot be supported from VEN, which is not adjacent to VIE. Instead, please support A TRI–TYR with A VEN; I’ll attack Turkish TYR. A RUH will hold, and A TRI will leave your centers untouched. A SER–BUD is useful pressure; please avoid vacating SER if that exposes your position.

A BUR will move to BOH, A RUH will hold, and A TRI will attack TYR with Italy’s support. I’ll keep French units out of WAR, MOS and STP. A WAR–GAL is legal and would help establish pressure toward VIE; please make that move if you can.

A BUR will move to BOH, A RUH will hold, and A TRI will attack TYR. I will not promise to leave VIE or TRI unopposed while you remain at 12 centers. I’ll avoid advancing into your other centers this spring.

No. With you holding 12 centers, a quiet Balkan line risks an immediate solo. I intend to contest your expansion this spring; I will not commit to leaving A SER and A VEN inactive while your units threaten the central line.
Agreed: A VEN will support A TRI–VIE, A GRE will move to BUL, and A SER will move to BUD. I’ll keep pressure on the Turkish line; please keep F TYS clear of Italian centers as promised.

Russia to England: The northern pact stands. A MOS and A WAR will stay out of DEN, HOL and SWE, and I will not enter the Baltic. Keep F NOR, F SWE, A KIE and F BAL off STP and my centres. Turkey at 12 is the danger; my WAR and MOS hold this spring, and I will decide fall moves once I see Turkish movement toward WAR or UKR.

Russia to France: I cannot attack GAL this spring; A WAR must hold to keep Russia alive, and A MOS stays put. Please confirm your A TRI and A TYR moves against VIE and that no French unit enters WAR, MOS or STP. If Turkey moves into UKR or WAR, I will counterattack in the fall. Let us coordinate exact orders next season.
I confirm: no Turkish unit will enter DEN, KIE, HOL, NOR, or SWE this spring. Keep F BAL, F NOR, and F SWE out of STP and my Balkan approaches; I will keep my fleets out of ENG and NTH.

A TYR will not enter VEN, and F ROM will not enter Italian centers this spring. I will defend my Balkan line and focus elsewhere; keep A SER and A VEN out of Turkish centers and do not support attacks on my units.
A ARM, A SYR, A UKR, and A VIE will stay out of WAR, MOS, SEV, and STP this spring. F BLA will not move to SEV. Keep A MOS and A WAR holding and away from my centers.

England to Turkey: You lead with 12 centres and I will not let you run away with the game unchecked. Keep your fleets out of ENG and NTH and your armies out of DEN, KIE, HOL, NOR and SWE. Tell me plainly whether A VIE and A WAR are heading north or south this fall.

England to Russia: Turkey is the threat to us both at 12 centres. Are A WAR and A MOS pushing on Galicia or Rumania this fall? Share your moves so we can coordinate. Our northern pact still stands from my side.

England to France: Please confirm F TYS stays out of the Channel and keep your armies off BEL and PIC. Turkey must be checked, and I will press against Turkish holdings where I can. Let us both keep our western truce while we pressure the Continent.

Turkey has 12 centers and is still the decisive threat. Can you support my A TYR–VIE with A VEN this fall, while A SER and A GRE pressure BUD and BUL? I’ll keep F TYS clear of your centers. Please confirm your exact orders.

Your A GAL is well placed to pressure Turkey. Please move A GAL–VIE this fall, or coordinate a supported attack there with my A TYR; Turkey must not keep expanding. I’ll keep French units out of WAR, MOS and STP. What will you do?

Turkey remains six centers from a solo. Please reconsider using F NOR and F SWE to pressure STP or the Baltic this fall; that northern pressure is crucial. I’ll honor our western truce and keep F TYS out of the Channel. Can you commit to a move against Turkey?

Let’s hit Turkey’s Balkan line together this fall. I can order A GRE–BUL supported by A SER; can you attack A VIE from MUN and support with RUH? I’ll keep A VEN out of French centers. Please confirm your orders.

Turkey still has 12 centers, and A WAR is vulnerable to coordinated pressure. Can A GAL attack WAR this fall, and can you keep Turkey from using A MOS to reinforce? I’m planning pressure on BUL from GRE, with SER supporting.

Turkey remains six centers from a solo. Can any English unit now threaten STP or another Turkish center this fall? I’m coordinating pressure on BUL from GRE and would welcome a northern attack; I’ll keep my units and fleets clear of English centers.

Russia to Turkey, Fall 1934: You hold 12 and your A MOS and A WAR-adjacent units are a clear threat. I need firm answers: will A SMY, A ARM or A SYR enter WAR, MOS, SEV or STP this fall? If not, I will keep A MOS and A WAR defensive. Name your moves for A VIE and A BUL.

Russia to England, Fall 1934: The northern pact stands. F NOR, F SWE, A KIE and F BAL must stay off STP, the Baltic and my centres. Turkey is the real danger to both of us. I am considering striking Galicia this fall; share your fall orders so we avoid any collision.

Russia to Italy, Fall 1934: Turkey at 12 must be stopped. Press BUD and TRI from SER and VEN. If Turkey moves toward WAR or UKR, I will counterattack Galicia. Tell me your fall moves so we coordinate pressure rather than collide.

Turkey will keep its units out of DEN, KIE, HOL, NOR and SWE, and our fleets out of ENG and NTH this fall. I need to break France’s eastern position: will you direct pressure against French-held BER or BEL, and keep your fleets away from my Balkan approaches?

Your A MUN and A TYR are gone, but our border remains dangerous. I propose a fall stand-down: keep A TRI and your other units out of Turkish centers and do not support attacks on VIE or TRI; I will not move against your centers this turn. What are your plans for A BEL and A PIE?

I’m willing to keep my units out of Italian centers this fall if you stop supporting French attacks on my position. Please keep A SER and A VEN from supporting pressure on VIE or TRI, and tell me whether F ION will stay clear of my fleets.

England to Russia: Northern pact stands from my side. I will keep F NOR, F SWE, A KIE and F BAL off STP and your centres this fall. Our fleets stay out of the Baltic-Russian waters. Turkey is the threat; if you strike Galicia with A WAR, tell me so we avoid collision. I need your word that A MOS stays out of SWE and DEN.

England to France: Western truce holds. F TYS stays out of ENG and I keep my armies off BEL, PIC and BRE. Turkey is the common threat, but my northern fleets are needed for home defence against Russia and Germany's ghosts. I will press Turkish holdings where practical. Keep A MUN and A TYR away from Holland and Denmark and we remain at peace.

England to Turkey: Noted. Keep fleets out of ENG and NTH and armies out of DEN, KIE, HOL, NOR and SWE and we stay at peace. I am not promising to attack BER or BEL for you, as France is also my neighbour. Your A VIE and A WAR heading north would change my assessment, so show me your hand.

England to Italy: My northern fleets cannot reach STP or the Balkans this fall without exposing my home centres. I will keep my units clear of your Adriatic and Greek interests. Press BUL hard; if Turkey's centres fall, I will consider a joint push next year. Keep F WES and F ION out of English waters.
Confirmed: F TYS stays out of the Channel, and my armies will stay off BEL and PIC. I’ll keep pressure on Turkey in the east; please make your promised move against Turkish holdings this fall.
A BEL and A PIE will not move into your centers this turn. I will not agree to stand down against VIE: Turkey’s 12 centers remain the decisive threat, and I intend to contest your expansion.

I’ll order A MUN–VIE with A TYR supporting MUN–VIE; A RUH cannot support VIE from its current position. Your A GRE–BUL with A SER support is useful—please proceed, and keep A VEN out of French centers.

England to France: Spring 1937. Agreed that neither of us wants a western war. My armies stay off BEL and the Channel this spring. I need your F TUS and A MUN kept away from Burgundy and Holland, and F NAF away from SPA waters. Your Balkan push against Turkey is fine by me.

I intend to use my eastern armies against Turkey, not Russia: A BUD will press GAL, and I have no spring move planned against MOS or WAR. I’m not targeting Italy this turn either. Germany is empty, but I won’t commit to leaving its territory untouched indefinitely; my priority is preventing Turkey from rebuilding.

I’ll keep A MUN out of HOL and F TUS out of your northern waters; F NAF is not moving toward SPA. A BUD will target GAL, putting pressure on Turkey’s Balkan line. I hope you use your northern fleets to contest Turkish positions rather than move against my centers.

I’m not planning to move A MUN or A MAR into VEN or TRI. A BUD will press GAL against Turkey. I can’t promise to leave your centers alone in future, but this turn I’m focusing east. Please avoid moves into French centers and use your Balkan units to challenge Turkey.

A BUD will press GAL; A MUN will not enter a Turkish center this spring. I will keep the pressure on your Balkan line, and I expect A BER and A GAL to stay out of French centers. I can’t agree to leave your position uncontested while you retain eight centers.

I’ll avoid Turkish centres this spring: A SER–BUD, A GRE–ALB, and F ADR–ION. I’m willing to coordinate against France, but your F GOL must stay out of TUS and your fleets clear of NAP and the Adriatic. Please use your position to contain France rather than threaten my coast.

My spring plan is A SER–BUD, A GRE–BUL, and F ADR–ION. I can pressure the Turkish line at BUL, but I won’t commit to helping you take more centres while you’re at 10. Keep A MUN and A MAR out of VEN and TRI, as agreed.

Russia to England: Thanks for holding F STP/NORTH and keeping fleets off my centres. I agree Turkey is the common threat, and France at 10 is the leader we must watch. Please keep F NOR, F SWE and A KIE clear of WAR, MOS and STP this spring. I will keep A MOS and A WAR defensive and tell you before any move toward Scandinavia. Let's agree STP returns to me once Turkey is checked, and share your autumn plans in time.
A GAL and A RUM will not move against WAR, MOS, SEV, or STP this spring. I cannot promise A UKR is involved; it is not among my units. Keep A WAR and A MOS defensive and do not contest Galicia.

I confirm A RUM, F BLA, and F CON will stay off Russian and English centres, and no Turkish unit will touch DEN, KIE, HOL, NOR, or SWE. Please keep your fleets out of the Balkans and Black Sea and do not support France.

I will keep F GOL and F ION out of TUS, NAP, and the Adriatic this spring. I am ready to coordinate against France, but need your A GRE and A SER to avoid Turkish centres. What pressure can you put on French positions?

A BER and A GAL will stay out of French centres. A RUM is defensive, and F GOL will not enter a French centre this spring. I cannot leave your army group free to expand; keep A BUD and A MUN out of Turkish centres and focus on the Russian or Italian fronts.

England to France, Fall 1937: France is at 10 and must be checked before it wins. I propose a concrete line: I hold F NTH and F NWG off BEL and ENG, and you keep A PIC and A RUH out of BEL and HOL. Will you commit to that and tell me whether F MAO will move toward SPA or POR?

England to Turkey, Fall 1937: You are at 8 and France is the runaway leader. Confirm in writing that A MUN and A VIE will not strike toward HOL, KIE or DEN, and that your fleets stay clear of NWG and NTH. In return I keep my fleets out of the Black Sea and Balkans. Are you willing to pressure France in the Alps or Munich area?

England to Russia, Fall 1937: I will hold F STP/NORTH this fall and keep F NOR, F SWE and A KIE off your centres. Keep A WAR and A MOS clear of SWE, DEN and NOR. If Turkey moves on MOS or WAR, I want to hear it first. Let us coordinate against France before it reaches 18.

France has no western move planned against English centres this fall. Please confirm your exact orders for F STP/NORTH, F SWE, A KIE and your Channel fleets. I propose we avoid each other’s centres and keep pressure on Turkey rather than open a western war.

Turkey remains the immediate obstacle in the Balkans. What are your exact plans for A BUL, A SER and A VEN? I can coordinate pressure from GAL, BOH and VIE, but need to avoid collisions with your moves. Please keep your units out of French centres this fall.

With our armies facing across the central front, tell me your intended orders for A MUN, A VIE, A RUM and A SEV. I will not leave your Balkan position uncontested, but propose we keep this fall’s fighting away from French centres and avoid needless moves against each other’s western positions.

France is at 10 and can win with eight more; you are also close at 9. Can you commit this turn to containing France rather than taking Italian centers? I will avoid English centers and waters. Please tell me your concrete targets, especially whether you can pressure Ruhr or Munich.

With you at 10, I cannot help you expand. Please keep A TYR and A MUN out of VEN and TRI, and avoid further Italian centers. Are you willing to direct your expansion against England or Turkey instead? I need your exact targets before I decide whether our border can remain quiet.

A ROM occupies my center, so I cannot treat our front as settled. Will you withdraw A ROM and keep F GOL and F TUN clear of NAP and the Ionian? I can discuss coordinated pressure on France, but only if you first give me security around Italy.

Russia to England, Fall 1937: France leads at 10 and must be stopped. Your F STP/NORTH is still on my centre, and I want it back once Turkey is checked. Let us coordinate: I will keep A MOS and A WAR off your Scandinavian centres. Will you move F NWG and F NTH against any French fleet in the North Atlantic or Channel? Share your autumn orders first.

France is at 10 and can still solo. I propose we coordinate pressure this fall: your fleets press French coastal centers while I use A MUN and nearby units against the French position. Please keep your fleets out of the Balkans and Black Sea; which French target will you attack?

France is the immediate solo threat at 10. Can we coordinate against its position this fall? I can press from A MUN and the eastern front; please use A VEN/A SER to pressure French units rather than Turkish centers. I’ll keep F GOL out of Italian centers and the Adriatic.

France is close to a solo, so I cannot agree to leave your front uncontested. What are A BOH, A GAL and A RUH doing this fall? I intend to contain your expansion; keep your armies out of Turkish centers and tell me where you plan to press.

England to Russia, Fall 1937: I hold F STP/NORTH this fall and keep F NOR, F SWE and A KIE off your centres. Your A WAR and A MOS must also stay off SWE, DEN and NOR. I will tell you before any move near Russian centres. Turkey and France both need watching; let us share intelligence on any French fleet entering the North Atlantic or Channel.

England to France, Fall 1937: I am not ready to commit to a fixed line yet. F NTH and F NWG will stay in the North Sea this fall, and I will not move against BEL or ENG unless you do. Keep A PIC and A RUH out of BEL and HOL, and tell me exactly what F MAO does toward SPA or POR. Your fleets in the Mediterranean are your business, but Channel moves will be watched.

England to Turkey, Fall 1937: I will keep my fleets out of the Black Sea and Balkans as agreed. In writing, I need A MUN and A VIE to stay clear of HOL, KIE and DEN, and your fleets clear of NWG and NTH. I am willing to discuss pressure on France through Burgundy or the Alps, but only after you confirm these moves in your orders.

England to Italy, Fall 1937: I will not move against your centres or waters this turn. Containing France is a real option for me, but I need to see it matched by your own pressure on the Alps and Piedmont. Keep your units out of ADR and the Ionian corridor toward my interests, and we can talk again in Spring 1938.

I’ll keep A PIC and A RUH out of BEL and HOL this fall. F MAO will not move toward SPA or POR. I have no western move against English centres planned; I’m concentrating on the eastern front. Please keep your fleets off French centres as agreed.

A BOH will hold the central line, A GAL will pressure RUM, and A RUH will stay out of the western centres. I’m not promising to leave your Balkan position alone, but I don’t intend to send these armies into your western centres this fall. What are your plans for RUM and VIE?

I’ll keep A TYR and A MUN out of VEN and TRI this fall, and I have no move into a French centre planned for your units to worry about. My immediate pressure is against Turkey, especially around RUM. Please keep A BUL and A SER from entering French centres.

My plan is A VEN–TYR, A SER–BUL, and A BUL–CON. A VEN will pressure your A TYR; the other two moves contest Turkish positions. I will keep my units out of French centers, but cannot promise to leave your units unchallenged while you remain at 10.

I can pressure France with A VEN–TYR. My A SER–BUL and A BUL–CON will also contest Turkish positions; I cannot leave my centers exposed while A ROM remains under your control. Keep F GOL and F TUN clear of NAP and the Ionian, and withdraw A ROM if you want a broader understanding.

Russia to England: Agreed on the surface. I will keep A WAR and A MOS clear of SWE, DEN and NOR. Your F STP/NORTH stays for now, but I expect it back once Turkey is checked. Please keep F NOR, F SWE and A KIE off my centres this fall. France is the real runaway, so I propose F NTH and F NWG move toward the Channel or Atlantic against French fleets in the autumn. Tell me your autumn orders before they are given.

I confirm A MUN and A VIE will not move toward HOL, KIE, or DEN, and my fleets will stay clear of NWG and NTH. I will press France from the Munich/Alpine front. Please put pressure on a French coastal centre and keep your fleets out of the Balkans and Black Sea.

I intend to use A MUN and A VIE to contain your central-front armies; A RUM and A SEV will remain focused east. I will not disclose exact orders, but I will not leave your army group free to expand. Keep your units out of Turkish centres.

A ROM is in my hands, and I won’t withdraw it this turn. F GOL will stay clear of TUS and F TUN will stay clear of NAP and the Ionian. France remains the immediate threat; if you pressure French units rather than Turkish centres, we can discuss a broader arrangement.

England to France, Spring 1938: Our western front has held, but France at 9 must not grow further unchecked. Confirm A PIC and A RUH stay out of BEL and HOL this spring, and that F ENG stays out of NTH and the North Sea. I will keep my Channel and North Sea fleets off BRE and PAR while you keep your word.

I propose coordinated pressure on Turkey this spring: my A UKR can move against RUM while your Balkan units press from the south. Please keep A BUL and A TRI out of French centres and tell me whether A BUL will support or contest my move into RUM.

With both of us at nine centres, a western war only helps Italy or Turkey. I propose we avoid each other’s centres this spring: my A PIC and A RUH stay out of BEL and HOL, and my F ENG stays out of the North Sea. What are your fleets planning?

I intend to press your Balkan line, not open a western front. What are your plans for A RUM, A BUD and A BER? I am considering a move by A UKR toward RUM; please keep your units out of French centres.

For Spring 1938, what are your plans for A BUL, F ADR, and the Ionian? I propose a temporary Balkan standstill: I will not enter CON or RUM if you keep your fleets out of the Adriatic and away from NAP. A ROM remains a serious problem; will you withdraw it?

You and England are both at 9, so I can’t support either side’s expansion. What are A MUN, A BOH, and A BUR doing this spring? I propose we keep the Italian border quiet while you focus on English or Turkish centers; I’ll avoid French centers if you keep your armies out of VEN and TRI.

What are your spring targets against France? With you both at 9, neither can be allowed to reach 18. I can press France from the south, but won’t commit to helping you take centers; please keep your fleets clear of the Mediterranean and Italian centers.

Russia to England, Spring 1938: Please state your spring orders for F STP/NORTH and your northern fleets before we move. Russia has only 2 centres and needs STP back. I will keep A MOS and A WAR off SWE, DEN and NOR. Will you support F NTH and F NWG against any French move into the North Sea?

France and England are tied at 9, so either can become the immediate solo threat. I propose we contain France together: I can pressure A MUN/A BOH from A BER and A BUD; please use your fleets against French centers. I’ll keep F CON, F AEG, and F ION out of English centers. Which target will you take?

With you at 9 centers, I cannot leave your central armies free to expand. I intend to use A BER and A BUD to pressure your central position; what are A BOH, A MUN, and A UKR doing? Keep your units out of Turkish centers and tell me whether you’ll avoid pressing RUM.

France is tied with England at 9 and remains a solo threat. Can we coordinate pressure on French units rather than Turkish centers? I can press from BER/BUD; please use A VEN or A TRI against the French central line. I cannot agree to leave Turkish centers exposed to A BUL or F ADR.

England to Russia, Spring 1938: My F STP/NORTH will stay put this spring and I will not move north into SWE, NOR or DEN with my own units. I will keep A KIE off your centres. Your A WAR and A MOS stay clear of SWE, DEN and NOR as agreed. I have no plan to support any French move into the North Sea; if France moves on NTH or NWG I will tell you.

I’ll keep A PIC and A RUH out of BEL and HOL, and F ENG out of NTH this spring. My focus is east; please keep your Channel and North Sea fleets off French centres as proposed. I won’t commit to leaving the eastern front uncontested.

A MUN and A BUR will stay clear of VEN and TRI; A BOH and A UKR are focused on the Turkish front. I’m willing to keep the Italian border quiet if A BUL and A TRI stay out of French centres. Please tell me whether A BUL will support pressure on RUM.

A MUN and A BOH will defend the central line; A UKR is positioned to contest RUM. I won’t promise to leave your Balkan centres alone, but I have no move planned into your western centres. What are A BER and A BUD doing this spring?

I won’t support A UKR–RUM; I can’t help you add another centre while you and England are tied at nine. I’ll keep A BUL and A TRI out of French centres this spring, provided A MUN and A BOH stay clear of VEN and TRI. Please direct your expansion toward England, not Italy.

I can pressure France from the central line, but I won’t expose Italy while A ROM is still a concern and you won’t leave Turkish centres open to A BUL. Keep your fleets out of ADR and away from NAP, and don’t move against ROM; I’ll use A VEN or A TYR to challenge France rather than move on CON or RUM.

I can keep F ADR out of the Ionian and away from NAP, provided you stay out of CON and RUM. A ROM is your unit, not mine, so there is nothing for me to withdraw there. I won't leave my Balkan centres undefended; let's keep this a mutual standstill while we contain France.

A RUM, A BUD and A BER will hold the eastern line; I won't leave RUM open to A UKR. I don't intend to move these units into French centres, but I will defend my position if you press the Balkans. What is A UKR's destination?

England to France, Fall 1938: Your A BEL, A PIC and A RUH sit next to my HOL, KIE and LON. Confirm in writing that none of them enter BEL, HOL or KIE this fall, and that F ENG stays out of ENG-adjacent Channel moves toward LON. I will keep F NTH and F HOL off BEL and BRE. Which French centre are you giving up to Italy or Turkey?

Our 9–9 deadlock gives Italy and Turkey room to grow. Keep your fleets off BRE and PAR, and I’ll keep F ENG out of NTH and my armies out of HOL. Can we maintain that line this fall while each contains the southern powers?

Turkey’s forces are stretched across the Balkans and central front. I propose we avoid French–Italian centres this fall while you press from BUL and I use A UKR to threaten RUM. Will you keep A BUL and A TRI out of French centres, and what will A BUL do?

The spring left our armies facing one another, and a direct fight helps England and Italy. I propose a limited pause: keep A BER and A BUD out of French centres, and I’ll avoid moves into your western centres this fall. What are your plans for A RUM and A SEV?

Your A RUM and F GRE are close to my Balkans, while I need room to grow. What are your Fall targets? I propose you keep A RUM out of SER and F GRE out of ALB; I’ll avoid CON and RUM this turn if you leave my centers and F ALB unthreatened.

What are A MUN, A GAL, and A UKR doing this fall? With you tied at nine, I need to know whether you intend to push toward Italy. Keep A MUN and A GAL clear of TYR and TRI, and direct your expansion against England or Turkey; I’ll avoid French centers.

What are your Fall targets against France? You and France are both at nine, so neither can be allowed a solo. Please keep your fleets out of the Mediterranean and avoid Italian centers; I can apply pressure on France if you are committing your forces against it.

Russia to England, Fall 1938: Your F STP/NORTH has held my centre long enough. Russia has only 2 centres. Please move it back to STP or support my retaking it once Turkey is checked. I will keep A MOS and A WAR off SWE, DEN, NOR. Tell me your autumn orders first.

Russia to Turkey, Fall 1938: Turkey holds 7 centres and my WAR and MOS are the only barrier to your northern push. Confirm that A RUM and A BUD stay out of WAR, MOS and SEV this fall, or expect A WAR to contest Galicia. Answer in writing before orders.
France remains tied with you at 9 and could still win. Will your fleets pressure French centres this fall? I’ll focus my eastern units on the central front and keep them clear of your centres.

We need a clear Balkan standstill while we contain France: keep A BUL and F ALB out of CON and RUM, and I’ll keep F BLA and F GRE out of your centres. Can you use A VIE or A TYR against the French central line?

You remain one of the two leading solo threats. What are A GAL, A MUN and A UKR doing this fall? I must defend RUM and my eastern centres, and I will contest any further French expansion toward the Balkans.

England to Russia, Fall 1938: My F STP/NORTH stays on STP this autumn as I hold the north, but I will not attack your centres and will not move into SWE, NOR or DEN against you. Keep A MOS and A WAR off those provinces too. Let us coordinate if Turkey or France threaten your position next year.

England to Turkey, Fall 1938: I will not move my fleets into the Balkans or Black Sea. Pressure on France is your business in the Alps and Burgundy. Keep A MUN and A VIE clear of HOL, KIE and DEN, and I will keep F NTH and F NWG clear of your centres. Show me your moves first.

England to France, Fall 1938: I will keep F NTH and F HOL off BEL and BRE this fall, provided A BEL, A PIC and A RUH stay out of BEL, HOL and KIE, and F ENG stays out of the Channel moves toward LON. Confirm this in your orders. I have no wish to see France or Italy gain more centres at Turkey's expense.

England to Italy, Fall 1938: I am not committing to war on France this autumn. My fleets will stay in the North Sea and Channel. I have no plan against your Mediterranean fleets or centres. If France moves on Italian centres, I may reconsider, so keep your Alpine pressure on A VIE and TYR forces firm.

A PIC and A RUH will not enter HOL or KIE, and F ENG will not attack LON. A BEL is already in BEL; I’m not promising to abandon a French centre. I’ll maintain the western restraint if your fleets stay off BRE and PAR. I’m giving up no centre to Italy or Turkey.

A UKR will press RUM, with A GAL positioned to support that pressure; A MUN will stay on the central line and out of Italian centres. I expect A RUM and A SEV to defend your eastern position, but won’t disclose every order. Keep A BER and A BUD out of French centres and we can limit the front.

A MUN and A GAL will stay clear of TYR and TRI. A UKR is focused on the Turkish front and may threaten RUM; I’m not directing my expansion against Italy this fall. If A BUL and A TRI stay out of French centres, we can keep the Italian border quiet.

I can use A TYR–MUN to pressure France’s central line; A VIE can also move toward BOH. I’ll keep A BUL out of French centres this turn, but need freedom to protect my Balkan position. Keep F GRE clear of ALB and avoid any move against Italian centres.

A BUL will stay out of French centres this turn; I’m not committing it to support A UKR–RUM. I intend to use A TYR against MUN to put pressure on your central line, so please keep A MUN and A GAL clear of TYR and TRI. I’ll avoid French centres if you do.

A RUM and A BUD will stay out of WAR and MOS this fall, and I have no move planned into SEV. I want to avoid opening a northern front while France remains the main threat; please keep A WAR from contesting Galicia.

A RUM will defend the Balkan line, and A SEV will hold; neither is moving into your centres this fall. I can accept a limited pause: A BER and A BUD will stay out of French centres if you keep out of my western centres. I will contest any move by A UKR toward RUM.

I can keep A RUM out of SER and F GRE out of ALB this fall, and I’ll leave your centres and F ALB unthreatened. Please keep A BUL out of CON and RUM as proposed. Let’s preserve the standstill while France remains a serious threat.

England to France, Spring 1939: Your A BUR, A BOH, A GAS and A RUH are close to my HOL and BEL line. Confirm none enter HOL, BEL or KIE this spring. In return my F HEL and F NTH stay off BEL, BRE and PAR. Will you give up any centre to Italy or Turkey instead of me?

England to Russia, Spring 1939: F STP/NORTH will not move north into SWE, NOR or DEN while your A MOS and A WAR keep clear of those provinces. I want to take a longer view: Turkey is the threat to both of us. Will you commit to holding WAR and MOS against Turkish or Italian pressure?

England to Turkey, Spring 1939: I keep my fleets out of the Balkans and Black Sea, and F NTH and F NWG off your centres. Your F TUN and F AEG are far from me. Show me your spring moves toward Italy or France before I commit anything further.

Italy is at 10 and can win with eight more; I propose we coordinate to contain it rather than fight over western centres. What are F NTH, F HEL and A KIE doing? I can keep A HOL and A RUH out of your centres if you keep your fleets off French centres.

Your forces are positioned to threaten my central line, while you need only eight more centres to win. What are A MUN, A MAR and A VEN doing this spring? I propose a mutual standstill at French–Italian centres while we address the other fronts; I will not leave my centres undefended.

Italy is the immediate solo threat at 10 centres. Can we coordinate pressure on its eastern flank this spring? Please tell me the intentions of A BER, A BUD and A RUM. My A BOH and A BUR can contest Italy, but I need to know whether you will avoid French centres.

What are your Spring targets for A GAS, A HOL, A RUH, and F GOL? I intend to secure my southern position and need to know whether you plan to contest MAR or move against PIE. Keep F GOL and your armies clear of Italian centers, and I’ll avoid further French centers this turn.

What are your plans for A ANK, A RUM, F AEG, and F BLA? I need to protect BUL and the Adriatic. I propose you keep your forces out of SER, BUL, and ALB, and I’ll keep A BUL out of CON and RUM this turn.

What are your Spring plans against France? Your northern fleets could pin French forces while I press from the south. Please keep your fleets out of the Mediterranean and away from Italian centers; I’m not committing to help you take French centers.

Russia to England, Spring 1939: Your F STP/NORTH has held my centre for two years. I am asking now: move it to GOL or NWG, or stand aside so I retake STP with A MOS this spring. Italy leads the race at 10 and must be checked. Answer before orders.

Italy is at 10 and can reach 18 before anyone else. I propose we coordinate to contain it: I can pressure A BUL and the Italian Balkan line; can you use A BOH/BUR and F GOL against Italy rather than contest my centres? Tell me your intended targets.

Italy is at 10 and the immediate solo threat. Will you commit your fleets to pressure Italian coastal centres, especially NAP, while I push against its Balkan position? I’ll keep my units clear of your centres. Which Italian target can you reach this turn?

Italy’s lead makes further expansion dangerous for everyone. Are you keeping A BUL and F ADR away from CON and RUM this turn? I can avoid a direct move against Italian centres if you confirm you will not press my Balkan centres.

England to Russia: I understand your need for STP. Italy is the real danger to us both. I will not move F STP/NORTH into SWE, NOR or DEN. I cannot promise to vacate STP this spring, but I will not attack your centres and will keep A KIE away from MOS and WAR. Let us coordinate on Turkey and Italy next year.

England to Italy: My fleets remain in the North Sea and Channel and I have no plans to enter the Mediterranean. I will not commit against your centres this spring. Keep your Balkan and Alpine forces focused on Turkey and France, and we can keep the peace.

England to France: I will hold F NTH and F HEL off BEL, BRE and PAR this spring, provided A BUR, A BOH, A GAS, A RUH and A HOL stay out of BEL, HOL and KIE. Confirm in your orders. I agree Italy is the leader and must be checked, but I will not give up any centre to contain it.

England to Turkey: I agree Italy is the leader and must be checked. My fleets are far from NAP and the Adriatic, and I will not enter the Balkans or Black Sea. Push your armies through the Balkans first, and I will consider naval pressure once your moves are clear.

I agree Italy is the urgent threat. A HOL and A RUH will stay out of your centres this spring; keep F HEL and F NTH off BEL, BRE and PAR. I cannot promise to give a centre to Italy or Turkey. Please use your fleets to contain Italy rather than pressure French centres.

With you at 10 centres, I will not leave French centres undefended or promise to keep my forces from contesting your expansion. I intend to coordinate against your Balkan position with Turkey. I will not disclose every order; avoid French centres if you want to prevent a direct French-Italian war.

Agreed: Italy is the immediate threat. I can use A BOH and A BUR to contest its central line and F GOL to pressure its western flank. I will keep my forces out of Turkish centres this spring; please press A BUL and the Italian Balkan line, and avoid French centres.

A MUN and A VEN will remain on the central front rather than enter French centres this spring. A MAR is focused on securing my southern flank; I have no plan for F GOL or Italian centres to be contested. Please keep A BOH clear of VIE and F GOL away from PIE.

I’ll keep A BUL out of CON and RUM, and F ADR away from your centres this turn. In return, keep A RUM out of SER and your fleets clear of ALB and the Adriatic. I’m not agreeing to a broader standstill, but I see no need for a direct clash this spring.

Russia to England, Spring 1939: Your F STP/NORTH is still sitting on my centre. I will hold WAR and MOS against Turkish or Italian pressure, but only if you act. Move F STP/NORTH to GOL or NWG this spring, or at least stand aside so A MOS can retake STP. Italy leads at 10 and is the real danger, so I need your answer before orders.

I intend to press Italy’s Balkan position, not your centres. F AEG can move against the Ionian while A RUM and A BUD contest the line; your best reachable target appears to be NAP with F NTH/F LVP only if you can reposition. Can you commit a fleet toward Italy this turn?

I will keep A ANK, A RUM, F AEG and F BLA out of SER, BUL and ALB this spring, provided A BUL stays out of CON and RUM and F ADR does not threaten my centres. I’m not promising a permanent standstill while Italy remains at 10.

I’m prepared to pressure Italy’s Balkan flank and will keep A BER, A BUD and A RUM out of French centres this spring. Please use A BOH, A BUR and F GOL against Italian positions rather than my centres; which targets are you taking?

England to Italy, Fall 1939: Your F TYS and F ION are far from my North Sea fleets, so I see no clash this turn. I still will not attack your centres. Tell me whether A SPA and A TYR are moving toward France or Turkey before I adjust my Channel and North Sea positions.

Italy now has 10 centers and is the immediate solo threat. I can pressure its central line from A MUN and A RUH; please use A BUL/A GRE and nearby forces against Italian-held Balkan centers. Confirm your targets, and keep A BER and A BUD out of French centers.

Italy is at 10 and must be contained. I propose we avoid fighting over French and English centers this turn: keep F NTH and F HEL off BEL and my other centers, while you use your fleets to obstruct Italian expansion. What are your fleet targets?

Your 10 centers make you the immediate threat to every other power. What are A TYR, A VEN and A TRI doing this turn? I will defend French centers and coordinate against further Italian gains; keep your units out of France if you want to avoid a direct war.

France is the immediate obstacle to both our growth. Please press its northern centres with your fleets and armies this turn, and keep your forces out of the Mediterranean and Italian centres. I can put pressure on France from the south; what are your targets?

France is coordinating against my Balkan position, so I need clarity on your intentions. Keep A RUM out of SER and your fleets clear of ALB and the Adriatic this turn; I’ll keep A BUL out of CON and RUM. Are you willing to pressure France rather than Italian centres?

Your cooperation with Turkey threatens my Balkan position. I’m prepared to keep this turn’s moves away from French centres if you keep A GAL and A MUN clear of my centres and do not support Turkish moves against SER or BUL. What are your plans?

Russia to England, Fall 1939: Italy now leads at 10 and is the real danger. Your F STP/NORTH is still on my centre. Please move it to GOL or NWG this autumn, or stand aside so A MOS can retake STP. I will keep A WAR and A MOS off SWE, DEN, NOR. Tell me your autumn orders before they are given.
